name: Pololu D24V22F5 5 V step-down regulator
description: Tiny 5 V synchronous buck module (up to 36 V in, about 2.2–2.5 A) with enable and power-good, a solid drop-in 5 V supply for small robots.

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Rated 2.2 A continuous at 24 V in (2.5 A typical max); less at higher input voltages.
Reverse-voltage protected; minimum input rises to about 5.8 V at 2.5 A.

terminals.name: PG
terminals.note: Open-drain power-good output: pulled low when VOUT falls below ~85% of nominal, high-impedance once VOUT rises above ~90%. Needs an external pull-up resistor.

terminals.name: EN
terminals.note: Enabled by default: 270 kΩ on-board pull-up to reverse-protected VIN. Drive below 1 V to enter low-power state (~5-10 µA per volt on VIN). Leave unconnected if unused.

terminals.name: VIN
terminals.note: Silkscreen 'IN'. Up to 36 V; effective minimum is VOUT + dropout (5.3 V headline minimum for the 5 V version).

terminals.name: GND
terminals.note: Square pad in the main 5-pin row, between IN and OUT.

notes: The five main pins are on one 0.1 in row in the order PG, EN, IN, GND, OUT, labeled on the top side. A 5x1 straight or right-angle header is included.
Dropout rises roughly linearly with load: about 0.25 V near 0 A to about 0.73 V at 2.5 A. These values are read from Pololu's dropout graph, not stated in text.
Has reverse-voltage protection (via a 40 V MOSFET, per the customization note), over-current/short-circuit protection, thermal shutdown and soft-start.
No-load quiescent current about 1 mA; with EN low, about 5-10 µA per volt on VIN.

Maximum continuous current depends on VIN and is thermally limited: about 2.5 A at 12 V in, falling to about 1.9 A at 36 V in (Pololu graph, still air, room temperature). The headline figure is 2.5 A.
Can get hot enough to burn you during normal operation.
Two 2.18 mm mounting holes for #2 or M2 screws.

summary: 5.3–36 V in → 5 V fixed, 2.2 A, 400 kHz
